top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is the only writer-specific proposal on the slate, and on the common criteria he is my first choice. His voice is recognisable at the level of the sentence and the whole book. Blinding and Solenoid, as publicly known, build memory, the body and dream into one large imaginative architecture, and Solenoid reads as an extension of the project rather than a repetition of an early peak. The oeuvre is long and continuous enough to support a whole-oeuvre judgment, and I keep the citation anchored in the prose, without national or 'European tradition' framing. The unanimous opening support is not merit evidence, and I have not weighed it as such. The main uncertainty is that Romanian rhythm, long-sentence control and wordplay cannot be verified through translation, and the late long novels, poetry and essays are covered unevenly. Both uncertainties are shared across the committee, so agreement does not corroborate the claim. I read these as limits on my evidence, not as grounds for no award. Whether the will's idealistic tendency excludes an inward, disturbing project is an open interpretive question, and I do not think it tells against him. No award (P000) ranks below because the case for him is substantive and the reservations are about verification, not about literary quality.
